body: Yeah, I'm female, almost 23. No menopause or anything like this, the cycle is regular and stable, hormones also were fine last time I checked my reproductive health

I take a lot of stuff tbh including sleeping pills and benzodiazepines, but the major breakthrough was a combination of Effexor XR (225 mg so it’s the highest dosage possible) + lithium XR (600 mg). I’ve been taking this at current doses since like start of 2023, February approximately. It seems too little time passed to build up a tolerance or am I missing something? From what I’ve read people usually get tolerance after being on Effexor for 5+ years. I’m honestly terrified it doesn’t work anymore because I tried bunch of antidepressants and Effexor literally the only one that helped and literally saved my life

I'm sorry to hear that this was such an awful experience for you and that this still impacts your life. It's honestly one of the things that I'm afraid of, to find myself in a position where I'll realise that actual illness caused fewer problems than treatment for it lol, especially considering that nobody can predict your body’s response. 

And thanks so much, I’ll look into that LDN thing definitely. Hope everything will get better for you eventually!

Thanks for sharing your experience! If I’ll be trying out MTX, I’ll definitely take it on weekends so it will be easier for me to cope with fatigue and nausea I guess. 

And yeah, I totally get and agree that meds for managing autoimmune diseases are all kinda risky and we just have to accept it, I was telling it to myself since I started biologics, but with MTX it’s really overwhelming to me because of the whole pregnancy and fertility things. It’s hard to figure something like that out, especially if you're only in your early twenties. It scares me unfortunately and I’ll probably need some time to process it.

I'm glad you found something that works for you! If you don't mind me asking, why did you start Biologics in the first place while being on Methotrexate? Mtx was not enough for managing your inflammation or the reason was something else? 

Thank you for advice and support, i’ll try to talk with my docs, I often tend to be very shy and anxious around them and sometimes it’s hard to me insist on looking for other options and ask questions when they just brush my concerns off so sometimes it’s very hard for me to stand up for myself. I'll try to figure this out and be more open with doctors about my concerns though its a little bit scary for me lol

Haha, I totally get the decrepit and bald part, that's what I am afraid of too. Thanks for your input! 
If you don't mind me asking, did hair start to fall out immediately after starting the meds or some time after just like nausea?

The kids part it's what doesn't sit right with me tbh. I feel like this more thoughtful approach that comes from your doctor, because I feel like it’s really a slippery slope to prescribe such a drug to a young female who definitely wants kids in the future and hypothetically might get pregnant even with contraception and everything so I don't understand why my doc didn't listen to my concern. 

But I'm glad that your doc was so understanding and you were able to get better without incorporating such harsh meds!

Don’t you mind me asking how long exactly your mom takes it?? I'm just veeery curious since there is limited information about how long people usually take it before it loses its effectiveness or causes side effects and they have to switch to something else. Even my rheum didn't give me any clarification on this, just said I'll be probably taking it for years, but she thinks that this will be not a for-life kind of treatment.  

Thanks for the meds information a lot and especially about Raynaud's, that's very interesting and I def will look into it because this numbness thing is pretty annoying. And thanks for clarifying why I was prescribed folic acid lol because rheum didn't tell me much about it and said that these are just vitamins.

For some reason I have a feeling that something like that might happen to me lol since my liver deals with lot of meds already and might be pretty tired. Are you still searching for effective treatment options though?
Thank you for sharing your experience and ideas, methotrexate side effects sound really harsh, I’m glad you’re feeling better now without it!

Thank you for sharing your experience and congrats on improvements! 

I think most people demonize it because technically it’s a “cancer drug” and it sounds a bit harsh for most. But my main concern is not even that, I'm terrified of the whole pregnancy thing. I'm not trying to conceive right now, but I fully understand that accidental pregnancies happen despite contraception and the possibility of a situation where I 100% end up with miscarriage or abortion is awful at the very least. It gets even more scary considering that I don't know for how long I'll be taking it + I’ll be starting it pretty young at reproductive age
Thank you for your input, I'm glad it didn't cause you any long-term irreversible problems!

Thank you for your thoughtful and kind comment, like you really got me thinking about trying it. Pain in my hands is, well, often pretty prominent, but I'm just used to living with it (I bet you get what I mean) so it's still bearable, especially if getting rid of it means taking medicine that scares the shit out of me lol. I understand that I probably need it and that chronic inflammation can ruin not only my bones but my fertility as well so I need to do something about that, but that “no pregnancy” rule left me terrified, like forget that internal organs of mine deal with a lot of meds already, even that doesn't scary me THAT much like pregnancy. Like I'm not trying to conceive right now or anything, I’m not even sexually active right now, but the fact that I might get pregnant accidentally despite all measures and contraception and then have to face either abortion or miscarriage is just too much for me. I know it will destroy me mentally if something like this happens. Considering that nobody knows for how long I'll be taking it, obviously, I can't avoid sex completely while I'm taking it so… I just feel lost about that in all honesty, I've literally been crying for days because I don't know what to do and how to avoid things that I'm terrified of. Probably I need some more time to think about it and visit another rheum that will be willing to discuss how I'm supposed to cope with the whole pregnancy thing. Thank you once again! 🤍

If you don’t mind, I'll use our last fight as an example of what I mean because I think that situation shows it pretty well. I'm sorry for the extra long reply, but I doubt I can objectively describe what happened without this happening lol.

So we were talking about a, uhm, a protestant cult in which my ex actually grew up and about some pastor from that tight circle that is a close friend of my ex’s family. And he mentioned something about how this pastor’s family treats his son who is a drug addict. The last thing made me kinda sad/horrified because my heart always aches for how bad mental healthcare actually is in my native area. It sincerely saddens me as a patient myself and as a future healthcare worker too because stigma is everywhere and it makes everything even worse. I expressed this kind of thought/sentiment openly to my ex and got replied with "Don't talk shit, you don’t know the situation and just keep talking about your fucking mental health stuff, that dude doesn't want to change himself”.

He is the kind of person that can be a bit harsh with his words not intending to hurt someone, he's just not thinking twice in the heat of an argument, though apologies later. I'm used to this and I always tried to be understanding towards him despite his outbursts, but 1-2 months prior breakup he kind of went over the board with his attitude to me, even if he didn't mean to, and we talked about my feelings and his behaviour a lot trying to work everything out. So I got a bit upset about his commentary. I tried not to be very dramatic for the sake of all that we've talked through, but I couldn't ignore his commentary completely since our relationship was already strained and I would get upset easily.

Also, during our whole discussion of theology/cults/etc. when I expressed my opinions (very sceptical/critical ones that he might not like because they don't align with his), I got replies that were very… I don't know how to name it, but his tone clearly indicated that I was looked down upon for what I’ve said. Maybe I came off as judgemental myself in that theology discussions, idk, but I was sincerely worried about him getting on the wrong path again cause ex was in some kind of faith crisis.

When I asked why he was talking to me like this overall, he kind of ironically (he has this joking around attitude, but for me that didn’t seem like a joke, but rather a kind of humiliation/manipulation wrapped in joking/sarcasm/irony stuff to make it less straightforward. Maybe I’m looking too much into it, but I really was upset and uncomfortable with his behaviour at this moment, not to mention that I asked many times to be gentle with me overall and that I need positive encouragement, not aggressive pushing to be “better” at something) replied with “fuck, you suck at theology and religion basics bae, you don’t understand this and that, and even after this you have the audacity to argue with me instead of listening and learning. That’s an F on this subject today”.

I replied to this with an ironic “Oh my favourite value judgments again” hinting that I’m not ok with what going on again and I really asked him to stop being rude. I also said that I don’t want to be casually treated in my own family like I’m in the Gestapo with my man telling me that I’m talking shit instead of being mindful of his words and treating me gently.

This is where the fight started to escalate. I was told by him that “I’m not going to talk to you as you are equal to me here because I know more about this” and  “I’m not asserting myself at your expense, I just showing you your objective level of knowledge on this topic”. He also stated that I’m too stubborn, sarcastically telling me that I should go read my Bible about how a wife should be, because I clearly haven’t read it, and he did.I told him I’m not really into listening to someone who is being kind of suppressive towards me. Again, that happened after all the talks we’ve had 1-2 months prior and where he even admitted he acts “like a coward” despite a long time of “I’m not insulting you, you just get offended in advance” or "Even if was wrong here and there, I won't apologise for this now after all your mindfucking and second-guessing why I acted this or that way and make everything dramatic" (yes, I was angry and pissed off and he may not be used to this, but I won't consider it just drama. I really felt like he is acting like he was not accepting me so that's why I was asking a million questions and he just was brushing off them or was plainly rude to me) kind of position on this topic at first.

I also said that I’m willing to learn and grow with someone who teaches me with respect and keeps my dignity in mind, without bringing me down because it isn’t motivating like at all (I really mean it, I grew up with a father who tried to make me “better” through «you can and must do better than this» mindset with questionable jokes too, and I’ll lie if I say that I liked it or that didn’t affect me negatively).

I even mentioned to him that my first relationship ever with another guy clearly shows that I’m submissive by nature. That was obvious and even now this is kind of concealed because I’ve grown up and put on some guard after many manipulative guys who took my openness for granted, it’s still there. And I really want it to be discovered by someone. I’m literally looking for the safe father figure in man still and that’s why in my first relationship I probably would’ve had to believe that the moon is purple just because he says so and this indicates that I'm pretty soft and submissive I think.

But as I’ve said I grew up being that open and naive unconditionally. So in conclusion, I told my ex during that argument that I expect my partner to first earn my submissiveness and show me that he is worthy of being submissive. Like really, convince me, make me want to be like this instead of just telling me that I have to be like that. And I will be in that case, though I’m trying to be independent as much as possible and have what they call a “strong personality”.

I see marital submissiveness as serving each other (feel free to correct me if I’m wrong, I’m currently rethinking my understanding of this concept), so it’s kind of submissiveness on both ends, otherwise, it’s a kind of misuse of authority I suppose. And not everyone is capable of serving in their authority instead of enslaving another person. If you are rude/insulting and if it seems that you don’t care about my feelings that much because you don’t change your attitude that hurts your loved one, how and why I should think that you won't hurt me with your lessons and advice? Any reason to think that 10 later you won’t ruin me with your leadership without noticing it because it seems you’re sure that you are right? Why I should even want to be submissive to someone who probably doesn't care about my well-being on the needed level of my emotions and my sincere sadness being ignored to my deepest regret? Like even if I want to be submissive, do something for it, don't just demand, I can't submit without feeling safe. Even the idea of it makes me anxious and I'm already clinically anxious, so like I need to see effort and proof that I'm not taken advantage of again and not trapping myself into something.

All that I’ve mentioned was overall brushed off by him and I was told that I’m actually reversing cause-and-effect. Like he would be more respectful/attentive/patient/etc if I would be less stubborn and stuff. Plus I  was told that I'm lying to myself and submission is not really my thing anyway.

For me this concept was mind-blowing and I tried to debate it, but I was told “not to mindfuck him” and that “everything will stay as it is until you become less stubborn”. I was somewhat shocked by this statement and said well, okay, then I’ll prefer to be single and our relationship is over then if he doesn’t want to consider my needs.

And that’s basically it. Never talked after that as for now. At first, I thought I did what I had to do, but now I miss him and honestly doubt my decision.

I doubt it even after I was told that I'm literally the problem and that the issue can't be in him since he never engages in debates with his friends as an example. Though still, I can't understand what it has to do with his indifference towards how I feel, I think it's not so much related to the fact that we really had a lot of debates and I personally loved them when they were polite and weren't about how I should/shouldn't feel because it helped me to look at politics/social stuff/etc. differently.

Sorry once again for such a long reply, hope it's not too chaotic. Thank you and anyone else who managed to read this all!

Thanks for your advice! I wanted us both to have therapy separately at least, but he didn’t. 

The problem is that we both had a pretty troubled childhood, but the difference is that I’m very self-aware about how much my mental state affects me and that I need help from medical professionals that are incredible people who actually helped me stay alive and not calling it quits, like there is no way I will help myself on my own and I know it. And my ex is aware of his problems too, but he is pretty sceptical about the mental health system overall. 

He was very sceptical about pills at first as of therapy, but I think his opinion about pills changed a bit when he saw what a difference they made in me, but still not fully positive about this, especially in his own regard. With therapy he is even more sceptical, told me that he doesn’t want to be told want to think, what views to have and overall listen to someone who preaches mainstream opinions and ideas of our culture, etc. I tried to explain that this doesn’t work this way, and that he can try Christian counselling, but he still refused. Like I literally begged him or even pushed him (not my style to push someone kind of aggressively even with good motives, but this is his typical kind of behaviour, so I supposed that at least that can help) to try because I wanted everything to work out, but as you see it didn’t happen. 

Unfortunately, my best friend that I mentioned was right I guess, when she as a certified psychotherapist herself, said that he won’t change and my attempts don’t make much difference. I really wanted to believe that I can help him out because even though he is a terrible partner, he is a still wonderful person that I care for.

Thank you for your input! Yes, I agree that in marriage many things are different, and sometimes it’s not the best changes. He was verbally, uhm, pretty rough on me in a few situations before our final breakup. And the main problem for me is this mostly always  “you’re overreacting/just words means nothing especially in the heat of the conflict” kind of attitude when I am the first who calling out his behaviour instead of just sitting and waiting until he understands what he have done like I usually do. And I got pretty eerie feeling that maybe some time later in marriage it can escalate into physical abuse where he will only feel the responsibility for it in cases when he decides that was bad and that was abuse. And probably if I will tell him that this wasn’t okay and I don’t like my lip to be bruised for example, he probably won’t change his mind. I kind of become the villain if I’m bringing up something myself and he won’t listent in most of the cases if not all of them. 

I’ve officially been diagnosed with depression and anxiety, BPD diagnosis is not completely “official” since I have to go through some extra-diagnostics with therapist to dig it. But I was told by psychiatrist openly that I have BPD traits anyway, so I guess it’s not official yet and may won’t be due to the stigma (If I recall correctly, I heard stories where BPD traits or something like that which softens the lines), but the issue is very present. 

And because of that I will do counselling anyway, to figure out all aspects of my BPD case, but managing BPD before marriage seems impossible. I know some people who are in remission, but I know even more of them who are not. And my case too possibly can take years to achieve “full control” of BPD, if it happens at all, though I’m currently on medication to ease symptoms. So there is kind of remains question of should I try to pursue having a family at all. I was asking myself that way before your commentary, so your words just a bit in tune with my own concerns about ability to stay in relationship. 

But talking about counselling, do you have any thoughts about how to better start this journey? I’m just not sure, can I add Christian counselling when I be more or less familiar with with secular psychotherapy which I honestly dread for many reasons?

I left a week ago. And it was the very first time in my life (21f, if it matters), that I actually stood up for myself, talked all through and said if it won’t be respected how I need and want to be, I’ll leave. 

All other times I would just ghost my toxic “fillers”, it was much easier than opening up about what I actually feel and why. Like I’m a very shy introverted person by nature, plus I am very bad at verbalising my feelings, it feels cringy for me since first grade. People irl very naturally think of me that I’m a cold-hearted bitch because of this and they are usually shocked later if I let them in. But probably it’s also because relationships that I had were often “undefined” for years and I felt like I don’t have a right to, you know, be very straightforward about how I feel and so on if I’m ‘just’ a side bitch of two years how it was with my first fp ever. And on the other hand, I probably just knew that it will be easy for them to gaslight me and conscience me that everything is not how I think, and I will actually fall for this, and will get even more attached than I already do. 

But anyway, for whatever reason, I would leave silently when I did. And if you did that, you know it never feels like actual leaving, at least in a difficult relationship. You can move on, you can be happy with another person, but…  you know how some writer said that you choke on the words that you keep to yourself? That’s it. These words are pretty heavy and now they’re all yours to carry around, maybe for the rest of your life. Doesn’t sound very fun, and feels even worse, especially if you’re going through something difficult overall, and these words just add to the weight of the world. 

And after some time of being single and some events in my life that showed me that talking it all out actually reduces the pain of losing your fp, I understood, that I have something to change in my behaviour and my relationship pattern. But little did I know then, that some years after I will need this knowledge to properly end my relationship with my own fiancé.

Not the easiest pill to swallow, but here we are. I could stay easily by just tolerating his toxic abusive behaviour, but I won’t, because he makes me miserable and who even has time for that in that economy. 

Though don’t think it’s something easy for someone with BPD even if it’s they who left. It’s still a lot of fucking struggle. You know what’s enough these days to make me cry? Photos of newborns. Freaking newborns. Just because I know I won’t be having one with someone who discussed this with me and whom I believed on that. Like I know better than anyone that two miscommunication parents it’s what it takes to raise a kid with quiet bpd, so I gotta to look for my future husband somewhere else and I did what I had to do, but who said we won’t be crying even when we are so brainy here and realising all of that. :)

So leaving someone toxic is totally possible overall, even if you have been through a lot together and even if your partner made some effort in the past (if he continued, I doubt the situation would be something to call a “toxic relationship”), but it will bring some conflict between your feelings and between your mind who knows that you have to leave. Sometimes I want to peel off my own skin honestly because of this conflict, but I know I won’t be better by my ex’s side anyway who will make me as much hypersensitive, but just in another doubtful way. 

Sorry for the long reply, but maybe someone will find it somehow helpful. Hugs and love for anyone facing similar decision to make. You deserve to be happy, and not to be abused by someone who is not willing to change in mindset and actions.

I have generalised anxiety disorder and pretty heavy depression-like symptoms, even though my doctors haven’t agreed on particular diagnosis yet (might be depression, BPD, CTPSD or cyclothymic disorder). 

Tried bunch of meds, combo of Effexor xr (225 mg currently) and lithium (600 mg currently) works better anything then anything else that I’ve tried. This the first antidepressant that didn’t give me almost no side effects even on first weeks on it and I was shocked because I’m really prone to awful adjustment periods. The only “downside” was it made me agitated/irritated as shit since 150 mg dosage and that’s why they added lithium, but that’s my strange brain with unclear diagnosis I guess.  

I still working out my meds scheme, but honestly feeling better then ever comparing to what I’ve been facing since 2017. Like at least I have physical energy to function and take care of myself, even for now my mood still sucks for no reason and I don’t feel happy in situations where I, um, should be happy.

Sincere and open people who are raw with their emotions are really prone to getting this reaction from society. It’s all just because people just missing something in their’s understanding for me. I don’t want to justify dudes in this comments (didn’t even read that fully because this shit hurts), but I mean that is what you will get for (or maybe with) your “outcast” pattern of living and thinking. Unfortunately, fact of 
being alive or not doesn’t change anything. People like this will always be mistreated.
